construct: Immortal time bias occurs when a period during which participants must remain alive and outcome-free in order to later be classified as exposed is incorrectly assigned to the exposed group's follow-up, creating an artificial survival advantage.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Classifying patients as treated based on a future treatment while follow-up starts earlier credits guaranteed pre-treatment survival to the treated group, which is immortal time bias.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Confounding by indication can coexist in observational treatment studies, but the stem explicitly defines a guaranteed survival interval before exposure classification; that design feature is immortal time bias. Lead-time and length-time biases require screening/detection effects; recall bias requires differential recall.
